newsitem.title: UK: Scots publican jailed for massacre charity theft.
newsitem.headline: Scots publican jailed for massacre charity theft.

text.p: A pub manager who fled to Spain with 800 pounds ($1,300) collected for victims of a gunman who massacred Scottish schoolchildren was jailed for 30 months on Friday.
Patrick Southgate, 49, vanished with the cash from a charity event at his pub organised to help families of 16 children murdered at Dunblane school in March. He also took the takings from the bar.

The father-of-five returned to Britain after 11 days on the run to turn himself in. He was sentenced at Southwark Crown Court in London by Judge Stephen Robbins who said: "I have regard to the revulsion felt about a person who can stoop so low as to steal charity money raised for Dunblane families."
Defence counsel Dora Belford said Southgate was attacked while in custody in prison over his "temporary abberation brought about by the pressures he was under."
